newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firm amid outage. storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firm amid outage. storm.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished firm Monday against Friday's levels amid ongoing tightness in spot supply, traders and marketers said.
"It's a just a shortage of power," said a Houston marketer, adding high fuel costs due to strong natural gas and residual fuel oil prices continued to keep some fossil fuel units off line.
Moreover, Rochester Gas and Electric Corp said it will take its 470 megawatt (MW) Ginna nuclear power plant out of service later this week to test its transformer.
The generating station in Ontario, N.Y., was running at 80 percent power to reduce stress on the transformer.
"Rochester is in a buying mode...They usually hold their own," said a Northeast trader.
The 510 megawatt (MW) Vermont Yankee nuclear station remained shut despite a scheduled restart this past weekend.

A weekend storm that pounded the Northeast with gusts and torrential rain limited the supply availability with a number of regional utilities still trying to restoring power service to their residential customers.
"There's nothing that affected the bulk market," said Bill Shepherdson, spokesman for the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) when asked whether the power deliveries were impacted from the storm.
In NEPOOL, peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $35.00-$37.00 a megawatt hour, up from Friday's range of $30.00-$35.00 for Monday delivery.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was valued at $21.00-$22.00, flat from Friday.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm electricity in the eastern part of the grid for Tuesday was pegged at $30.00-$32.00, unchanged from Friday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP was at $14.50-$15.00, compared with offers near $17.00 on Friday.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday delivery were discussed at $20.00-$23.00, unchanged from Friday.
Western NYPP electricity for non-firm, off-peak delivery during Tuesday's light load hours was assessed at $14.00-$14.75.
